slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward
in a group (and finally join in)

Stand with your body open to the group. Not half turned toward the exit, not hiding behind someone's shoulder. Feet pointed in, drink in one hand. People make room for someone who looks like he belongs.
Laugh at other people's jokes for real. You don't need your own punchline. Being a great audience gets you included way faster than trying to be the funniest guy in the circle.
Add to the story instead of starting a new one. Someone talks about a trip? "Wait, did you go to the night market?" Building on their topic pulls you in without hijacking the conversation.
Have something to add to any topic. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. When the group drifts to ancient Rome, space or old movies, you're not standing there lost, you're right in it.
slides.texte_sophia: Have something to add to any topic. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. When the group drifts somewhere new, you're right in it.

slides.texte_overlay: Ask the group a question, not just one person. "Okay, best concert you've ever been to?" Everyone answers, the energy goes up, and suddenly you're the one who got the whole circle talking.
Stop waiting for the perfect moment to speak. It never comes. Say something at the first gap, even if it's small. "Same, that happened to me last week." Short is fine. Silent all night isn't.
Stick close to one person you know at first. Warm up with them, then drift into the bigger group together. You don't have to walk into every circle alone. Even confident guys bring a wingman.
